column2: For every \(\varepsilon > 0\) there exists \(\delta > 0\) such that \(0 < |x - a| < \delta\) implies \(|f(x) - L| < \varepsilon\).
The distance between x and a on the number line.
The limit ignores the value at a itself. f need not be defined there.

column1: Why does sgn x have no limit at 0?
column2: With \(\varepsilon = 1\), any window around 0 holds values 1 and -1, which cannot both be within 1 of one L.
